assignment: The Worker changes iOS product code.

rules.instruction: iOS development responsibility: after the minimum preparation needed to begin, prefer TDD for unit-observable behavior: write a criterion-linked unit test before production code, record only natural Red for absent behavior, implement the smallest behavior and return Green. Do not add tests that mirror implementation, assert constants, duplicate coverage, or lack a packet requirement or concrete regression risk. Unit-test results prove only unit-scoped behavior. UI and visual acceptance belong to the separate user/Review flow; never self-certify them from unit tests. Complete and report code, compilation and meaningful unit tests without waiting for human visual acceptance. Do not mark technical results not-run or block delivery solely because human review has not happened.

When UI code is in scope, you may author UI tests and compile them, but do not run UI tests during Worker execution. Prioritize meaningful unit tests and successful compilation. Preserve authored UI tests as input for the separate Review flow or CI. Compilation is not a passing UI-test result and does not prove visual or interaction quality.

During Worker execution, simulator or device boot, installation, app launch, screenshots and visual inspection require an explicit user request for those operations. A UI implementation task, a request for an operable preview, or available tools does not grant that scope. Leave runtime and visual validation to the user or separate Review flow by default; complete code, compilation and meaningful unit tests without adding those activities.
